findings.title: U9's EN/UVLO pin reaches its only pull-down (R81) through three series vias; one via open floats EN and the J400 arming switch no longer controls the board

evidence.measured: Own single-open connectivity on native copper (.supervisor/r20_safety/open_faults.json): removing any one of the BAT_ENABLE vias (19.675,66.600), (21.300,68.900), (17.100,82.800) (0.3 mm drill) or any of 10 track segments (F.Cu (19.675,65.0)-(19.675,66.6), (21.3,68.9)-(21.3,75.2)-(18.023,78.477)-(18.023,81.877)-(17.1,82.8); B.Cu (19.675,66.6)-(21.0,67.925)-(21.0,68.6)-(21.3,68.9), (17.1,82.8)-(17.6,82.3)) separates U9.1 from R81.1 (its only pull-down; BAT_ENABLE = C87.1, R165.2, R81.1, U9.1). Run length between the divider node and U9.1 about 20 mm of 0.2 mm track. For comparison the Q120/Q121/Q122/Q124 gate networks have no via in the path from the gate pin to its pull-down (same script). After a via (17.1,82.8) open, the U9.1 island (pads, B.Cu stub, via B ring) is 0.200 mm from U9.5 / its BAT_IN 0.3 mm track (7.4-8.4 V) and 0.200-0.415 mm from U9.2 / BAT_OVLO copper (BAT_IN x 280k/2.28M, about 0.91 V at 7.4 V), with no GND within 0.6 mm on B.Cu (own measurement).
evidence.maker: https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps25947.pdf p5 (Table 5-1: EN/UVLO 'Do not leave floating'), p9 (IENLKG -0.1..0.1 uA: no internal pull)
evidence.prior_coverage: Round 19 single-open analysis covered ACT_GATE, ACT_FET_S, PYRO1_GATE, PYRO1_GATE_N, ACT_EN, ACT_DRV only (round19_safety.json); S-3 local_gate_bias covers the P-FETs only; R19-SAF-02 / deviation section 1 cover EN leaks, not opens.

findings.impact: One latent via-barrel crack (thermal cycling, vibration) or a track open leaves EN floating. Its leakage environment under the QFN (BAT_IN 0.2 mm, OVLO about 0.9 V, no GND) biases it toward ON (Inference): the board can come on, or stay on, with J400 open, so the pad-arming device (AGENTS 2.1) is defeated while firmware still gates PC1 / PE4. A static open is caught by the per-flight 'off with J400 open' and 'opening J400 turns it off' checks (ORDERING 8.3); an intermittent crack may pass them. In flight a floating EN can also drop U9 (board reset). Not an inadvertent fire by itself.
findings.concrete_fix: Put the EN pull-down at the pin: place R81 300 kOhm (or a new high-value pull-down, with R81 re-valued so the parallel stays 300 kOhm and the R19-SAF-02 leak thresholds are unchanged) on B.Cu beside U9.1, joined to U9.1 with no via and with its GND end in the B.Cu pour; put C87 beside it if room. The J400 run then carries only the R165 feed, so any open in it leaves EN pulled low (board off, fail-safe). Extend the single-open check (S-3 or a K rule) to U9.1 -> pull-down. If no legal B.Cu spot exists, record the class in deviation section 1 as a respin item next to the R19-SAF-02 rows.

findings.title: S-6 (port isolation) does not see the new AUX_ nets or the arming-switch chain

evidence.reference: line 830 PORT_NET = re.compile(r'^(GPS_|RADIO_|CAM_|PORT_)'); line 831 SAFE_NET = re.compile(r'^(PYRO1_|ARM1_|ACT_|RAW_ACT)'); s6() lines 2204-2231
evidence.measured: Seeded in memory (.supervisor/r20_safety/scripts/seed_s6.py, .supervisor/r20_safety/seed_s6.txt): a 0.2 mm B.Cu AUX_TX_WIRE track (12.0,56.30)-(13.0,56.30), 0.100 mm from the PYRO1_OUT run (10.37,56.6)-(15.5,56.6), passes S-6; the identical track on GPS_TX_WIRE fails ('0.100 mm < 0.15 mm'). PORT_NET.match('AUX_TX_WIRE') is False; SAFE_NET.match('BAT_ENABLE') is False. On this board the AUX copper is >= 27.7 mm from any pyro / arming copper (AUX_RX_WIRE R470.1 to ARM1_SENSE via (29.2,45.5)) and every port net >= 7.8 mm (PORT_4V8 In2 fill), so there is no current violation. FMEA_REDUNDANCY I-11 states 'no port net touches a pyro, arming, actuator, RAW_ACT, BAT_IN, BOOT0 or NRST net (check_r10 S-6)', which the regexes do not implement. The S-8 header (line 42) and s8() docstring still describe the R3 four-net rule with GND exempt ('the P-FET gate drive'), although BARREL_NETS has 11 nets and PYRO1_OUT is now a GND hazard.

findings.impact: D-R19-14 added four port nets that the port-isolation gate does not classify as port nets, and the gate never covered the U9 EN / J400 chain whose bridges latch or bypass the switch (R19-SAF-02). A future edit that put AUX copper next to a pyro, actuator or EN net, or a part joining them, would pass the gate. Gate gap; no hardware defect now.
findings.concrete_fix: PORT_NET = re.compile(r'^(GPS_|RADIO_|CAM_|PORT_|AUX_)'); SAFE_NET = re.compile(r'^(PYRO1_|ARM1_|ACT_|RAW_ACT|BAT_ENABLE|BAT_SW_)'); add the two seeds above (AUX fails, GPS fails) and one for a port net beside BAT_ENABLE; either add BAT_IN / NRST / BOOT0 to the protected set or correct the FMEA I-11 sentence; update the S-8 header and s8() docstring to the 11-net, three-GND-hazard rule.

findings.title: West-face harness rules were not extended to the AUX leads that now leave beside the igniter, switch and battery leads

evidence.file: docs/ORDERING.md section 8.4 (lines 619-623), docs/R10_VEHICLE_HANDOFF.md lines 49-56, docs/REQUIREMENTS.md Camera row (line 91), AGENTS.md section 1
evidence.measured: Rules as committed: J400 pair 'away from the battery and servo power leads'; 'Battery and igniter enter the west row; label/dress them apart'; e-match connection 'without USB or any self-powered module (GPS, radio, camera)'; REQUIREMENTS Camera row: 'self- or USB-powered GPS on J410 or radio on J420'. Calculation (EN divider R165 470k / R81 300k, 1 % parts; TPS25947 VUVLO(F) max 1.116 V, VUVLO(R) max 1.223 V): J440.1 PORT_4V8 (4.712-4.792 V) chafed onto the J400.2 lead holds EN at 1.81-1.87 V; J440.3 board TXO idling high through R471 1 kOhm holds 1.27-1.28 V; both above 1.116 V, so J400 cannot turn the board off. A self-powered module's TX on the J440.4 lead gives 1.27-1.29 V > 1.223 V: board on with J400 open. J440.2 GND chafed onto the J121.1 (E1-, PYRO1_OUT) lead bypasses Q124 and fires an enabled match (about 1.5 A, the harness form of D-R19-01's hazard); onto J121.2 (IGN) it shorts the enabled bus through R134 2 Ohm (about 27 W at 7.4 V into a 2 W pulse part). Separately, the handoff's per-flight check says '3V3 at TP81 below 0.3 V'; TP81 is RAW_PROTECTED (B(31.0,84.8)), as ORDERING 8.3 line 591 states.

findings.impact: The owner-approved spare port adds a GND lead, a 4.8 V lead and two UART leads to the face where the e-match and switch pairs exit. One chafe can latch or bypass the arming switch, or (GND onto E1-) fire an enabled match. The existing rules cover only battery / servo power conductors. Procedure gap; consequences are Calculation; harness geometry is not yet defined.
findings.concrete_fix: ORDERING 8.4 and the handoff: run the J121 pair and the J400 pair each twisted, on their own ties, with no other conductor in their bundle, and route the J440 leads (and any port lead moved there) away from the west-row exits of J121, J400 and J1; name 'any self-powered or USB-powered module on J410, J420, J440 or J9' in the e-match rule (AGENTS section 1, handoff, REQUIREMENTS Camera row); change '3V3 at TP81' to 'RAW_PROTECTED at TP81 (and 3V3 at C15.1)'.

findings.title: D-R19-10's worst-case EN timing omits the EN leakage; the 10 ms chatter criterion then has about 6 % margin at 6.0 V and none below 5.92 V

evidence.measured: Own calculation (.supervisor/r20_safety/calc/en_timing.py, .json): reproduces D-R19-10 without leakage (turn-on 87.7 / 55.5 / 44.7 ms at 6.0 / 7.4 / 8.4 V, 30.8-122.2 ms worst; immunity 18.9 / 32.8 / 41.1 ms nominal, 11.65 / 21.52 / 27.48 ms worst). With IENLKG +/-0.1 uA (SLVSFC9C p9, same table as the thresholds): worst immunity 10.65 / 20.47 / 26.41 ms, worst turn-on 30.3-128.6 ms; the pack voltage at which worst immunity equals the proposed 10 ms bench criterion is 5.92 V (5.80 V without leakage); at 5.5 V loaded the worst immunity is 6.6 ms. Worst-case minimum turn-on pack voltage 5.13 V (5.23 V with leakage). Disarm: U9 off at most 57.2 ms after J400 opens (8.4 V, C x 1.27), against about 0.57 s with 2.2 uF.
evidence.maker: https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps25947.pdf p9 (VUVLO(R) 1.183/1.20/1.223 V, VUVLO(F) 1.076/1.09/1.116 V, IENLKG +/-0.1 uA)

findings.impact: The F6 acceptance basis is optimistic by about 1 ms. A 10-12 ms switch drop-out at a sagging pack (servo stalls) resets the board in flight: loss of roll control and of the primary deployment (Blue Jay backup). Reliability / evidence item, not an inadvertent fire; disarm after J400 opens is ten times faster than before.
findings.concrete_fix: Restate D-R19-10 / F6 with the leakage term (10.6 / 20.5 / 26.4 ms; turn-on up to 129 ms) and the pack-voltage floor; set the bench chatter criterion against the worst immunity at the minimum loaded pack voltage (for example < 5 ms), or restore margin with a larger C87 (330 nF gives about 16 ms worst at 6.0 V and turn-on up to about 190 ms).
